To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the aerodynamic performance of a flapping wing can be predicted based on the instantaneous shape deformation of the wing, that the instantaneous wing deformation can be predicted based only on the aerodynamic and acceleration-related damping forces, and that both the aerodynamic performance and wing deformation can be understood based on the interplay between the aerodynamic and added mass forces.

the aerodynamic forces and the wing deformation of an insect-size flapping wing in hovering can be predicted by an analytical model that includes the effects of the added mass and aerodynamics damping.

(i) the lift of an insect-scale flexible wing in hovering is determined by the instantaneous angle of attitude, which depends on wing deformation, and (ii) the wing deformation and lift of an insect in hovering are determined by the interplay of acceleration-related and aerodynamics damping forces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a simple model for instantaneous aerodynamic forces and wing deformation of insect-scale flapping wings in hover.
the analysis of flexible wings of insects in hover and the prediction of aerodynamic performance.
the analysis of flexible wing aerodynamics and the development of a simple model for the prediction of lift.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a simple model can predict both instantaneous lift and shape of an insect-scale flexible wing in hover.
wing deformation is a result of the aerodynamic force and the wing shape is a consequence of the wing deformation.
the aerodynamic performance of a flapping wing is determined by the interplay of aerodynamic damping and acceleration-induced forces, which are both related to the unsteady flow around the wing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the instantaneous lift of an insect-scale flexible flapping wing can be predicted by the instantaneous angle of the wing.
the instantaneous wing kinematics can explain the resulting aerodynamic forces.
the wing shape and aerodynamic performance of an insect-scale wing in hover are strongly coupled and can be predicted by our simple model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the instantaneous aerodynamic performance of a flexible flapping wing can be predicted in hover by considering the combined effect of added mass, aerodynamic damping, and wing deformation.
the wing deformation can be predicted from a simple model, which is a significant advance for the analysis of insect-scale flapping wings.
the instantaneous aerodynamic forces can be accurately predicted by a simple model based on the instantaneous wing kinematics.
